transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
I came in because my mind feels foggy. I can’t keep my place in my old cataloguing notes, and even simple decisions—what to do next—I just get stuck.
Aside from the fogginess, how has your mood been lately?

Most days I just sit at the kitchen table feeling low. It’s like the color has gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books—I used to enjoy looking through them, but now they just make me feel heavy.
Have you ever experienced a period in the past where you felt this low?
Yes. I’ve been feeling this way most days for about three months now. It seemed to start around the time I began getting ready to leave the library.
Before these past three months, had you ever experienced another time in your life when you felt depressed or low like this?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that felt like this.
How has your sleep been over these past three months?
I go to bed tired, but I keep waking up around four in the morning. Then I just lie there thinking about what I’m supposed to do with myself now.
Have you had any recent physical illnesses, head injuries, or medical problems?
No, I haven’t had anything like that recently.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past three months?
Yeah. I have to remind myself to eat lately. My wife notices I leave my rice and soup half-finished, and I never used to waste a meal like that.
With feeling this low, have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean by thoughts of harming myself. I do feel very low, but I haven’t really thought about that specifically.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt the opposite—unusually energetic, elated, or full of ideas, needing much less sleep than usual?
Right after I retired, I had a few days where I felt almost too bright and excited. I’d get sharp with my family over little things, like if they asked me to slow down.
How long did that period of feeling unusually bright and excited last?
The whole change lasted about three weeks, after that first rush from retiring wore off.
